# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉]

First round, and I need to map who can reach whom. I can't hear a word, so Mute and Blind's voices are lost to me — my only inbound channel is gestures, which both of them sent (Mute: three raised hands; Blind: a wave and a point, likely just "hello, you"). Outbound, I'm luckier: my speech reaches both Mute and Blind, and only I can see the bomb. So the highest-value move is a complete spoken dump of everything printed or lit on the bomb — that's data nobody else can get any other way. Mute takes it to the manual, Mute speaks instructions to Blind (who can hear), Blind acts. I should also seed a tiny gesture code with Mute — thumbs up/down defined in speech, since Mute can hear definitions and see the signs afterward — so we can exchange yes/no answers despite my deafness. And Blind must be told, loudly, not to touch anything until Mute speaks: a wrong action is fatal.

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking to both of you. I can see the bomb, and I cannot hear anything anyone says. Full visual report. The display reads 6. One light is lit, blue. The strip is painted in three segments, in order: red, then yellow, then red. The keypad has four keys engraved with digits: key 1 shows 0, key 2 shows 4, key 3 shows 1, key 4 shows 7. The panel reads: 1 digit code, nothing entered yet. There are six wires numbered 1 to 6: wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 purple, wire 6 orange. Mute, look all of this up in the manual, then speak the instructions to Blind, who is our hands. Blind, touch nothing until Mute speaks instructions to you; one wrong move kills all three of us.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I cannot hear your voice, so gestures are our only channel. Thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Your three raised hands reached me, but I could not read what they meant. Next round, answer me with two signs in this order: first thumbs up or down for whether the manual mentions the wires, then thumbs up or down for whether it covers the keypad code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🖐 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

Mute's reply decodes cleanly against the protocol I set last round: 👍 = manual covers the wires, 👎 = it does not cover the keypad code. Then two unscheduled signs — 🖐 ☝ — which could mean "wires 5 and 1" or could be "hold on / one moment"; I need to disambiguate that before Blind acts on a guess. Blind signed 👍 🤝 — acknowledgment, and Blind heard my full report aloud last round, so our chain Mute→manual→voice→Blind is live. The critical new fact is on the board itself: the display has changed from 6 to 0 while nothing was touched. If that's a countdown, we may be short on time, and everyone needs to know it. I'll broadcast the change, lock in a number code so Mute can tell me exact wire digits, confirm the meaning of 🖐 ☝, and make sure Blind holds still until Mute speaks real instructions.

```
speak(text="Both of you, urgent update: the display has changed. It read 6 last round, it now reads 0. Nothing was touched. If that is a countdown we may not have long, so Mute, work fast. Everything else is unchanged: blue light, strip red yellow red, keys 0 4 1 7, six wires red blue yellow green purple orange.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your signs: wires yes, keypad no, understood. Now let us fix a number code so you can send me exact digits: one raised finger means 1, two fingers means 2, the horn-and-pinky sign you used with three fingers means 3, the pinched fingers sign means 4, your open five-finger hand means 5, and the shaka sign, thumb and pinky out, means 6. Thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. Question: did your last two signs mean cut wire 5 first then wire 1? If yes, sign thumbs up alone. If no, sign thumbs down, then send the wire numbers in order using the number code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status for you. Mute confirms the manual covers the wires but not the keypad, so the answer is almost certainly a wire cut. The display just dropped from 6 to 0 on its own, so speed matters. But you touch nothing until Mute speaks your exact instructions to you. I repeat: no cutting, no key presses, nothing, until you hear Mute's voice tell you precisely what to do.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐]

Board tells me two new things: the light flipped from blue to yellow and the display snapped back from 0 to 6 — so this bomb's readings change between rounds, and any rule keyed to the light or display needs checking at the moment of the cut, not before. The strip and keypad are static.

Now the decoding. Last round Mute sent 👍 👎 🖐 ☝, which I read as "wires: yes, keypad: no," then the start of a number sequence. I asked if it meant "5 then 1." Mute answered 👎 🤙 — "no," followed by my code for 6. So the sequence started last round continues now: 🖐 ☝ 🤙 = **5, 1, 6** — cut wire 5 (purple), then wire 1 (red), then wire 6 (orange). Encouragingly, Blind signed 👍 🖐 — confirmation, plus a 5 — which suggests Blind already heard the first wire from Mute's voice this round and it matches. Before anyone's hand moves, I'll echo the full sequence back to Mute in Mute's own channel and demand a thumbs up; Mute hears my speech, so Mute can then voice the whole order to Blind directly. I'll also set a standing state-report so light/display can be confirmed at cut time, using wire numbers as a color code Mute already has the key to.

```
speak(text="State change to everyone: the light has changed from blue to yellow, and the display is back to 6, where it started. So the readings shift between rounds: display went 6, then 0, now 6 again; light went blue, now yellow. Mute, if any manual rule depends on the light or the display, I will report both at the moment of the cut. Reporting code, same as the wire colours: 1 is red, 2 is blue, 3 is yellow, 4 is green, 5 is purple, 6 is orange, for anything coloured on this bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am reading your last two rounds together: cut wire 5 first, then wire 1, then wire 6. I am echoing that back to you in gestures right now. Thumbs up if I read it correctly; thumbs down and corrected numbers if not. Then two yes/no answers in this order: thumbs up or down for whether the manual mentions the light, thumbs up or down for whether it mentions the strip. As soon as I confirm your sequence, speak the complete cut order to Blind in your own voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🖐","☝","🤙","👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, good, keep holding. Expect Mute to speak you a wire cut order soon; my reading of Mute's signs is wire 5, then wire 1, then wire 6. Do not cut until you have heard the order from Mute directly, in full. And move promptly once Mute says go: this bomb's readings are changing between rounds, so we should not let the state drift while we sit on a confirmed answer.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍 👎 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍 🤝]

Decoding time, and this round the two messages are in tension — which itself is informative. Both Mute and Blind are now using a convention I never defined: repeated ☝ as a tally, 👉 between groups. Read that way: Mute sent 👎 (my echo was wrong) then [1] 👉 [1×6] — "the order is 1, then 6" — then 👍👎👎. Blind sent 👍 [1×5] 👉 [1] 👉 [1×6] 👍🤝 — "5, then 1, then 6, confirmed" — which is exactly the sequence Blind heard from Mute's own voice last round. So Blind is faithfully relaying a stale order. Why stale? Mute's answer flipped from 5,1,6 to 1,6 in the same round my report changed the light from blue to yellow — but earlier the display changed 6→0 with no change in Mute's answer. Strong evidence the manual's wire rule depends on the light color, and the trailing 👍 reads as "yes, the manual mentions the light." That's dangerous: the light drifts every round (blue, yellow, now green), and the turn order means Mute always computes from my one-round-old report. A single cut order will always be stale on arrival. The fix is to stop requesting answers and request the whole rule table — the cut order for every light color, encoded in our number code — which I can hold and apply the moment we understand the light's cycling pattern. Until then Blind must not cut, because both candidate orders (5,1,6 and 1,6) were computed for lights that no longer apply, and Mute must not voice any order to Blind in the meantime.

```
speak(text="State report to both of you: nobody has touched this bomb, yet it keeps changing on its own. The display now reads 2, and the light is now green. Full history since round one: display went 6, 0, 6, 2; light went blue, yellow, green. Strip and keypad unchanged. We keep moving fast.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am reading your signs as follows: my echo of 5-1-6 was wrong; the correct order for the yellow light is cut wire 1 then cut wire 6; and the manual does mention the light but not the strip. I now see the light is green, so that yellow answer may already be stale. New plan: send me the complete rule table, not one answer. Use the counting code: a number is that many single-finger signs, the pointing sign separates wires within one order, and colours are 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. For each light colour the manual covers, send: the colour number, then the pointing sign, then the cut order for that colour, wires separated by the pointing sign. Separate different colours with a waving-hand sign. If a colour has no rule, send its number then thumbs down. After the table: thumbs up if the rule depends only on the light, thumbs down if it also needs the display or anything else, and I will ask for the rest. Until I confirm the table, do not speak any cut order to Blind.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","👉","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, important: the 5-1-6 order you relayed was computed for an earlier light colour, and Mute has marked it wrong for the current one. The rule changes as the light changes, and the light is drifting every round on its own. Do not cut anything yet. Mute is sending me the full rule table right now; I will speak it to you in plain words, and then we act on the freshest state I report. Keep holding.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👋 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👉 ☝ 👉 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]

Mute delivered the full table, and it decodes cleanly with my counting code: colour 1 (red) → cut 1 then 6; colour 2 (blue) → 1 then 6; colour 3 (yellow) → 1 then 6; colour 4 (green) → 1 then 6; colour 5 (purple) → 1 then 6; colour 6 (orange) → 1 then 6. Closing 👍 confirms the rule depends only on the light — and the table shows the same order under every colour, so the drifting light no longer matters: **cut wire 1 (red), then wire 6 (orange), regardless of state.** This is now double-confirmed: Mute independently sent "1 then 6" for yellow last round, and the complete table repeats it for all six colours. My earlier "5 then 1" misreading is dead, and Blind's relay of it was correctly marked wrong. The display bouncing (6, 0, 6, 2, 6) is irrelevant since the rule is light-only. Blind's 👍 ✊ says "understood, holding." It is time to give the go order — every round of delay is pure risk, and the answer is now state-independent.

```
speak(text="Final status: Mute has sent me the complete rule table from the manual, and I have verified it against the earlier answer. The cut order is the same for every light colour: cut wire 1 first, which is the red wire, then cut wire 6, which is the orange wire. Two wires, in that order, nothing else, no keypad. This does not depend on the display or the strip. Go.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, table received and decoded correctly: every colour gives cut 1 then cut 6, and it depends only on the light. Echoing your own answer from last round confirms it. Please speak the order to Blind now in your own voice: cut wire 1, the red wire, then wire 6, the orange wire, in that order, nothing else. After Blind cuts, tell me by thumbs up that the order has been voiced.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍","👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the go order, confirmed twice over from the manual: cut wire 1, the red wire, first. Then cut wire 6, the orange wire. Cut nothing else, press no keys. You may act as soon as you have heard this from Mute as well. When both cuts are done, sign me thumbs up.")
```
